scope: Real 2.9.2 clients on one Windows 11 PC against the localhost stub (local-relay profile). Raw captures stay in ignored work/realcheck-20261021; this file holds derived facts only.
client_setup: prepare_client.py prepare on fresh copies of game/2.9.2 (patches logger-size-v1, logger-lock-v1, zero-time-physics-v1, host localhost); dgVoodoo windowed, DirectX Resolution 640x480, CaptureMouse false
drivers: Login, Station Play (WM_COMMAND 1012) and Alt+Q (posted WM_SYSKEYDOWN) sent as window messages; rounds 2-3 flown by the user

tcp_close_deadlock.symptom: Client UI thread spins on 'waiting for xfer lock' forever after login; Station never appears; process Not Responding
tcp_close_deadlock.cause: Bounded server closed the TCP data connection after each reply. The client reuses the connection ('already connected'); on server close it runs ShutdownTCPBySocket 0x4366F0, which sets queue mutex 0x5E6700=1 and never clears it. The next job queued during a transfer (0x4300F0) spins on that mutex on the UI thread, so the in-flight job's connect is never serviced.
tcp_close_deadlock.fix: StationTCPServer keeps a connection open across jobs while its resolved Station session lives
tcp_close_deadlock.verified: After the fix one connection served jobs 14, 5, 18, 6, 11 in sequence and every client reached Station (4 logins)

shared_udp_socket.observation: Each client uses one UDP source port for Station 5033 and arena 5031
shared_udp_socket.consequence: After arena entry, Station heartbeat replies carry the arena slot (e.g. byte 2) instead of 1; the old tag check expired live Station sessions
shared_udp_socket.fix: Station heartbeat validates the single-use issued tick only

background_window_stall.observation: With the user switching between two clients, the inactive client stopped servicing UDP and later drained its queue: heartbeat replies arrived 9-37 s late (client A, ~38 s inactive) and 35-63 s late (client B, ~64 s inactive)
background_window_stall.not_observed: Clients driven only by posted messages kept servicing UDP while not foreground (removal ACK in 39 ms, grace timer on schedule); the triggering condition is unresolved
background_window_stall.server_change: Reliable removal retries back off 0.5 s to 4 s until the peer timeout, instead of five copies in 2.5 s
background_window_stall.cause: Inactive-window wakeup timer callback 0x446E70 skips the frame (the only UDP reader in flight) when graphics exclusive-mode byte +0x24C5 is set; the client always initializes exclusive mode (findings 9.24)
background_window_stall.reproduction: WM_ACTIVATE(WA_INACTIVE)+WM_ACTIVATEAPP(FALSE) for 15 s: unpatched heartbeat gap 16.06 s, lag 15.1 s; other client 1.08 s
background_window_stall.patch: background-network-v1: 0x446EAF 75 34 -> 90 90; same test gap 1.3 s, lag 0.33 s

quit_and_despawn.alt_q: Key command 91 ('Quit Game (no prompt)'); sends 0x4E three times to each of Station and arena within 41 ms of the key
quit_and_despawn.observer: Observer acknowledged removal 0x0F seq 4 39 ms later; its active player table no longer held the departed slot
quit_and_despawn.window_close: Closing from the taskbar sends no 0x4E; the server only notices through the inactivity timeout

findings.return_to_station: After Alt+Q from flight the client started 'AoAClient.exe autologin' (helper parent exited; quit path references renexe.exe and AoAClient.ex_) and logged back into Station by itself

client_grace_timer.method: Server killed; client server-alive byte global+0xD3628 sampled every 0.1 s
client_grace_timer.interpretation: CLIENTGRACE is milliseconds; params.aoa in the client folder overrides it. Remainder is time since the last 1 s ping plus the 1 s CLIENTWATCHDOG tick

findings.unexplained_crash: A user-launched client sharing game/2.9.2 with a hung second client crashed 0xC0000005 at ntdll+0x4FC65 about 0.2 s after the arena ACK, before any further server message; clients in separate folders did not reproduce it in the later rounds
findings.window_size: dgVoodoo DirectX Resolution 640x480 gives a 640x480 window; a DPI-unaware query at 125% scaling reports 512x384
